title: An exact functor carries the triangle of a short exact sequence to the triangle of the image sequence
statement:
Let $F:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$ be an exact functor between abelian categories, and let $F_D:D(\mathcal C_1)\to D(\mathcal C_2)$ be the triangulated functor induced by applying $F$ termwise to complexes, with its shift isomorphism $c_K:F_D(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D(K)[1]$ and its natural isomorphism $\varphi_A:F_D(A[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(A)[0]$ for objects $A$ of $\mathcal C_1$ placed in degree $0$ [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ be a short exact sequence in $\mathcal C_1$, with the distinguished triangle $A[0]\xrightarrow{f}B[0]\xrightarrow{g}C[0]\xrightarrow{w}A[0][1]$ of [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle], $w$ the morphism constructed there from the mapping cone $C(f)$ of $f$ (the inverse of the quasi-isomorphism $q:C(f)\to C[0]$ followed by the canonical morphism $C(f)\to A[0][1]$, with the sign convention of that construction; Stacks 0152 writes it $-p\circ q^{-1}$), and let $w':F(C)[0]\to F(A)[0][1]$ be the morphism constructed in the same way for the short exact sequence $0\to F(A)\xrightarrow{F(f)}F(B)\xrightarrow{F(g)}F(C)\to0$ of $\mathcal C_2$ (exact since $F$ is exact). Then
$$
\varphi_A[1]\circ c_{A[0]}\circ F_D(w)=w'\circ\varphi_C,
$$
so that $(\varphi_A,\varphi_B,\varphi_C)$ is an isomorphism of triangles [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift] from $\bigl(F_D(A[0]),F_D(B[0]),F_D(C[0]),F_D(f),F_D(g),c_{A[0]}\circ F_D(w)\bigr)$ to $\bigl(F(A)[0],F(B)[0],F(C)[0],F(f),F(g),w'\bigr)$ (the first two squares commute by naturality of $\varphi$).
